research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: direct official GOV.UK, Planning Inspectorate, HM Land Registry and Planning Data verification; 2026 currentness where present, enforcement-vs-permission, lawful-development scope, permitted-development/prior-approval limitations, condition status, local-land-charge coverage/provenance, taxonomy-vs-occurrence and exact-parcel fail-closed gates. Not parcel-level accuracy.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification plus repository duplicate searches

official_sources.name: Enforcement and post-permission matters
official_sources.fact: Government guidance updated 6 May 2026 defines planning-control breaches, enforcement notices, stop notices, breach-of-condition notices and related remedies.
official_sources.gate: A complaint, investigation or notice type must not be converted into proof of an extant breach, final liability or current parcel development status without the exact notice and its live status.

official_sources.name: Lawful development certificates
official_sources.fact: Guidance distinguishes certificates for existing and proposed lawful development and states that certificates establish lawfulness only for planning-law purposes and specified circumstances.
official_sources.gate: A lawful-development certificate is not a general planning permission and does not remove other legal, building-regulation, listed-building, licensing or permitting requirements.

official_sources.name: Use of planning conditions
official_sources.fact: Planning guidance explains legal/policy tests for conditions and warns that development in breach of conditions can be unlawful and subject to enforcement.
official_sources.gate: A permission record cannot be treated as fully implementable unless relevant pre-commencement and other live conditions are checked and their compliance status is known.

official_sources.name: Flexible options for planning permissions
official_sources.fact: Guidance distinguishes section 73 applications to vary or remove conditions from section 96A non-material amendments and other amendment routes.
official_sources.gate: An amendment route or application does not prove that the operative permission, approved plans or conditions have actually changed until the decision is verified.

official_sources.name: When is permission required?
official_sources.fact: Guidance explains permitted-development rights, prior approval and use classes, including that rights are subject to limitations, conditions and local exclusions.
official_sources.gate: Potential permitted development or same-class use cannot be promoted to lawful development without checking the exact right, limitations, Article 4/local constraints and any required prior approval.

official_sources.name: Fees for planning applications
official_sources.fact: Guidance describes fee treatment for application types including prior approval and lawful-development certificates.
official_sources.gate: A fee category identifies an application route only; payment or fee calculation is not evidence of validation, approval or lawfulness.

official_sources.name: Making an application
official_sources.fact: Guidance distinguishes full, outline, reserved-matters, condition-discharge, amendment, lawful-development and prior-approval application routes.
official_sources.gate: An application type or valid submission is not planning permission; outline principle, reserved matters and discharge stages must remain distinct.

official_sources.name: Determining a planning application
official_sources.fact: Guidance sets decision-notice requirements and notes current consultation directions affecting specified decisions, including the 2026 direction.
official_sources.gate: Committee resolution, officer recommendation or consultation step is not the issued decision notice or final permission status.

official_sources.name: Permission in principle
official_sources.fact: Permission in principle separates location, land use and amount from technical details; development cannot proceed until technical details consent is granted.
official_sources.gate: Permission in principle, brownfield-register inclusion or site suitability must not be promoted to full permission, TDC grant or deliverability.

official_sources.name: Planning appeals procedural guide for applications on or after 1 April 2026
official_sources.fact: Planning Inspectorate guidance updated 16 July 2026 covers appeal rights and procedures for applications submitted on or after 1 April 2026.
official_sources.gate: The existence of an appeal right or submitted appeal does not establish that the original decision is overturned or permission is granted.

official_sources.name: Appeal against a planning decision
official_sources.fact: GOV.UK explains appeals against refusal, objectionable conditions and non-determination.
official_sources.gate: Appeal eligibility or submission is procedural status only; the appeal decision and any resulting conditions must be verified separately.

official_sources.name: Enforcement appeal information sheet
official_sources.fact: Planning Inspectorate information updated 23 March 2026 states enforcement appeals must be received before the notice effective date.
official_sources.gate: An enforcement appeal does not by itself quash, suspend permanently or resolve the underlying planning status; exact appeal and notice status are required.

official_sources.name: Enforcement appeal submission changes coming soon
official_sources.fact: Planning Inspectorate announced that from June 2026 planning and enforcement appeals are submitted through the Appeal a Planning Decision service.
official_sources.gate: A digital submission channel is process evidence only and says nothing about the merits or outcome of an appeal or parcel.

official_sources.name: HM Land Registry Local Land Charges Programme
official_sources.fact: HM Land Registry programme guidance updated 20 July 2026 explains phased migration of local land charges and that registered charges include planning conditions and other restrictions.
official_sources.gate: National migration status does not prove a specific authority has migrated or that a search is complete; authority coverage and search date must be checked.

official_sources.name: Practice guide 79 Local Land Charges
official_sources.fact: HM Land Registry guidance explains local land charges can include planning conditions, enforcement notices, listed buildings, conservation areas and TPOs and may affect land even if not registered.
official_sources.gate: Absence from a search result must not automatically be treated as absence of every obligation; registration coverage, search scope and other enquiries remain relevant.

official_sources.name: HM Land Registry local land charges search results
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 22 July 2026 explains differences and interpretation for authorities moved to the national Local Land Charges service.
official_sources.gate: A search-result format or migrated dataset is not itself evidence that every planning/highways/building matter relevant to development is contained in that result.

official_sources.name: Search for local land charges
official_sources.fact: The GOV.UK service searches restrictions such as planning conditions, highways agreements, TPOs and conservation areas but states not all local-authority data is on the service yet.
official_sources.gate: No result from an uncovered or incompletely migrated authority must not be treated as a clean parcel legal-status result.

official_sources.name: Planning Data permitted development right
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 236 permitted-development-right categories, collector run 23 July 2026, with some MHCLG-created experimental data.
official_sources.gate: A PDR category is taxonomy, not proof that the right applies to an exact parcel or that its conditions and prior-approval requirements are satisfied.

official_sources.name: Planning Data permitted development right part
official_sources.fact: Planning Data lists 21 PDR part categories and notes MHCLG-created experimental provenance.
official_sources.gate: Part/category classification must not be treated as occurrence, applicability or lawful-development evidence for a parcel.

official_sources.name: Planning Data planning condition
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 5,605 planning conditions from one provider and states the dataset is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
official_sources.gate: Platform condition records are not authoritative proof of the complete live condition set or discharge/compliance status for a permission.

official_sources.name: Planning Data planning application condition
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 5,305 planning-application conditions, collector run 22 July 2026, with MHCLG-created provenance pending authoritative replacement.
official_sources.gate: Application-condition data must not be promoted to final permission conditions or compliance status without the authoritative decision notice and subsequent approvals.

official_sources.name: Planning Data planning application type
official_sources.fact: Planning Data lists 41 application-type codes including lawful development, condition variation/discharge and multiple prior-approval routes.
official_sources.gate: Application-type codes are schema categories and do not establish that an application exists, is valid, approved or relates to a target parcel.

official_sources.name: Planning Data planning permission type
official_sources.fact: Planning Data lists seven planning-permission types, including full, outline, reserved matters, permission in principle and technical details consent, from authoritative sources.
official_sources.gate: Permission type is categorical metadata; exact permission reference, decision, dates, conditions and parcel relation are still required.

official_sources.name: Planning Data planning permission status
official_sources.fact: Planning Data lists permissioned, not-permissioned and pending-decision status categories from authoritative sources, collector run 23 July 2026.
official_sources.gate: Status vocabulary is not evidence that any particular site actually has that status unless linked to authoritative site/decision records.

official_sources.name: Planning Data planning decision
official_sources.fact: Planning Data currently reports 0 planning-decision records, 0 providers and no collection attempt on the public dataset page.
official_sources.gate: Zero platform rows means NO_DATA and must not be interpreted as absence of planning decisions for a parcel or authority.

official_sources.name: Planning Data planning decision type
official_sources.fact: Planning Data currently reports 0 planning-decision-type records and no collection attempt on the public dataset page.
official_sources.gate: Zero platform rows means NO_DATA; decision-maker type must be read from authoritative application/decision records where relevant.

official_sources.name: Planning Data local area requirements
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 335 local-area-requirement records from one provider and notes MHCLG-created provenance pending authoritative replacement.
official_sources.gate: A generic or platform validation list cannot be assumed current for an authority or application date without checking the live local requirements.

official_sources.name: Planning Data brownfield land
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 37,666 authoritative brownfield records, collector run 23 July 2026, with fields including permission status and permission type.
official_sources.gate: Brownfield-register presence or a permission-status field does not replace the exact live decision notice, conditions, expiry/implementation and parcel geometry checks.

official_sources.name: Planning applications in England January to March 2026
official_sources.fact: The official statistical release reports 2026 quarterly counts for permission-in-principle and technical-details-consent decisions.
official_sources.gate: National/authority statistics describe aggregate activity and must not be converted into parcel-level approval probability or demand.

official_sources.name: Planning Data developer agreement
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 12,775 developer agreements from 78 providers with mixed authoritative/MHCLG-created provenance and collector run 21 July 2026.
official_sources.gate: Agreement presence, draft data or platform linkage does not prove obligations are executed, current, discharged or applicable to an exact parcel unless the authoritative agreement is checked.

official_sources.name: Planning Data developer agreement contribution
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 39,325 developer-agreement contribution records from 77 providers with mixed provenance.
official_sources.gate: A contribution record or formula is not proof of the final liability, payment status, indexation, trigger or delivered infrastructure for a parcel.

official_sources.name: Planning Data developer agreement transaction
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 49,891 developer-agreement transaction records from 73 providers with mixed provenance and collector run 21 July 2026.
official_sources.gate: A transaction record must not be interpreted as full obligation discharge, infrastructure delivery or parcel readiness without agreement-level reconciliation.
